- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or adjust downward after 2–3 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.10) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 2–5% buffer to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not continue rising unless sentiment shifts.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period volatility; adjust last 5–7 days of forecast downward if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows increasing positive sentiment, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% per day of rising sentiment.
- When sentiment is high and price is near support level, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% if price is below 10% of 30-day high.
